title: ZO Skin Centre
summary: I brought four clinic locations into one browsing and booking experience, so patients could compare treatments, practitioners and results without losing their place.
goal: The existing site split the clinic experience across separate locations and made booking harder than it needed to be. The redesign had to create one clear path from treatment research to consultation.

targetUsers.label: Patients
targetUsers.description: People comparing treatments, practitioners, results and clinic locations before they book.

targetUsers.label: Dermatologists
targetUsers.description: Practitioners whose credentials and experience need to be easy for patients to evaluate.

discoveryNote: The clinic manager pointed to three recurring problems: booking took too much effort, each location felt separate, and the proof patients looked for was scattered across the site.
insights: Separate location pages made comparison harder and forced patients to restart their journey.
Treatment information, practitioners, reviews and results worked better when they supported the same decision.
The booking path needed to stay visible and work cleanly on a phone.
competitorAnalysis: The comparison focused on how clinic sites bring treatment details, practitioner credibility, results and booking into one journey.

userFlows.name: Book a Consultation
userFlows.steps: Homepage → Select service → Choose doctor → Fill booking form

userFlows.name: Compare Treatment Options
userFlows.steps: Homepage → Treatment → Practitioner and results → Choose clinic

wireframes: Started with low-fidelity layouts to settle the relationship between treatments, locations and booking.
Moved into high-fidelity prototypes after the main path was clear.
visualDirection: Used a quiet, premium visual language with generous space and restrained medical cues.
Stayed close to the parent brand while giving the clinic a clearer identity of its own.

keyScreens.name: One front door for every clinic
keyScreens.description: Placed all four locations on the homepage so patients could compare them without moving between separate sites.

keyScreens.name: Proof close to the decision
keyScreens.description: Brought practitioners, reviews and before-and-after results into the treatment journey instead of leaving them in isolated sections.

keyScreens.name: A shorter route to consultation
keyScreens.description: Kept booking actions visible and made the form easier to complete on mobile.

title: Ibadat
summary: I designed a daily prayer app around three moments: checking prayer times, finding trustworthy duas, and silencing the phone automatically inside a mosque.
goal: The brief was not to add more features to another prayer app. It was to remove small interruptions from daily practice while keeping prayer times and religious content dependable.

targetUsers.label: People building a daily prayer routine
targetUsers.description: Need dependable prayer times, useful reminders and authentic duas without a cluttered experience.

targetUsers.label: People praying at a mosque
targetUsers.description: Need their phone to stop interrupting prayer without remembering to change settings every time.

discoveryNote: Working with the client clarified a simple product principle: every feature had to earn its place in a daily religious routine, where trust and low effort matter more than novelty.
insights: Prayer times needed to be dependable and local; anything less would undermine the whole app.
Dua sources needed to appear at the point of reading, not in a separate reference area.
Mosque silent mode had to work with almost no effort from the user.
competitorAnalysis: The comparison focused on prayer-time setup, source visibility for duas, custom collections and silent-mode controls.

userFlows.name: Set Up Prayer Times
userFlows.steps: Open app → Confirm location → Review prayer times → Set reminders

userFlows.name: Find and Save a Dua
userFlows.steps: Browse collection → Open dua → Read translation and source → Save

wireframes: Mapped the prayer-time, dua and feed experiences in low fidelity before adding visual detail.
Used high-fidelity prototypes to test hierarchy across the main daily-use screens.
visualDirection: Used a calm palette, clear type and restrained Islamic references rather than heavy ornament.
Kept navigation and controls simple enough to scan quickly across a wide age range.

keyScreens.name: Prayer at a glance
keyScreens.description: Made today's times and the next prayer immediately visible, with reminder controls close by.

keyScreens.name: Silent mode without another ritual
keyScreens.description: Turned mosque silent mode into a simple, location-aware setting instead of another manual task to remember.

keyScreens.name: Trustworthy duas in context
keyScreens.description: Kept Arabic, transliteration, translation and source references together, with saving available in the same view.

title: Alokito Teacher
summary: I redesigned Alokito Teacher and added a job marketplace, giving teachers one place to build skills and find work while schools got a direct hiring path.
goal: The product had to do two connected jobs: help teachers choose and buy courses, and help institutions hire them. The redesign needed to make both paths clear without turning the site into two separate products.

targetUsers.label: Teachers
targetUsers.description: Need a clear way to compare courses, understand pricing and move from learning to job opportunities.

targetUsers.label: Institutions and schools
targetUsers.description: Need a focused way to publish roles and review applicants with relevant training.

discoveryNote: The client brief brought two experiences together: an education business selling courses and a new marketplace connecting teachers with schools. The information architecture had to make that relationship understandable.
insights: Course discovery, pricing and job search needed to feel connected because the same teachers moved between them.
The job marketplace needed distinct paths for teachers and institutions.
Individual courses and higher-value packages needed to be easy to compare without crowding the homepage.
competitorAnalysis: The comparison focused on how education platforms organise course discovery and how job portals separate search, application and hiring tasks.

userFlows.name: Choose a Course
userFlows.steps: Homepage → Browse courses → Compare details and price → Enrol

userFlows.name: Find and Apply for Work
userFlows.steps: Job marketplace → Search and filter → Review role → Apply

userFlows.name: Hire a Teacher
userFlows.steps: Institution portal → Publish role → Review applicants → Manage applications

wireframes: Used low-fidelity layouts to connect the homepage, course catalogue, pricing and job marketplace.
Refined the high-fidelity prototype with direct client feedback.
visualDirection: Balanced an energetic education brand with clear type, controlled colour and predictable page patterns.
Designed the main teacher journeys mobile-first.

keyScreens.name: One path from learning to work
keyScreens.description: Connected course discovery, pricing and job opportunities instead of presenting them as unrelated destinations.

keyScreens.name: Faster job search for teachers
keyScreens.description: Designed search, filters and application steps around the information a teacher needs to decide whether a role fits.

keyScreens.name: A separate hiring path for institutions
keyScreens.description: Gave schools a focused route to publish jobs and manage applicants without mixing those actions into the teacher experience.

title: TaxRise
summary: I redesigned TaxRise's marketing site around clearer service paths, stronger proof and a consultation flow that makes the next step obvious.
goal: Tax relief is already hard to understand. The website added another layer of friction through inconsistent pages, scattered proof and unclear next steps. The redesign had to make the path to expert help feel simpler and more credible.

targetUsers.label: People looking for tax relief
targetUsers.description: Need to understand their options, judge whether the company is credible and know how to start.

targetUsers.label: Internal teams (SEO and marketing)
targetUsers.description: Need repeatable page structures they can extend for new services, content and campaigns.

discoveryNote: Conversations with stakeholders, SEO and marketing surfaced one shared problem: the site had grown page by page, without a consistent route from a tax question to a consultation.
insights: Service pages used different patterns, so the next step changed as people moved through the site.
Customer stories, case results and enrolled-agent credentials were separated from the moments when people were deciding whether to trust the company.
Marketing needed a page system that could support new campaigns without redesigning each one from scratch.
competitorAnalysis: The comparison focused on how tax-relief sites explain services, place customer proof and repeat the consultation action.

userFlows.name: Find the Right Service
userFlows.steps: Homepage → Explore tax problem → Review service → Start consultation

userFlows.name: Evaluate Trust
userFlows.steps: Service page → Customer story or case result → Team credentials → Consultation

wireframes: Started with low-fidelity page structures for services, proof and consultation.
Refined the high-fidelity system with stakeholder feedback across roughly 30 screens.
visualDirection: Built a consistent visual system for type, colour, components and page hierarchy.
Used customer stories, case results and team credentials as part of the information hierarchy, not as decoration.

keyScreens.name: A consistent service-page system
keyScreens.description: Created a repeatable hierarchy for complex tax topics, supporting proof and a clear next step.

keyScreens.name: Trust before conversion
keyScreens.description: Brought customer stories, case results and enrolled-agent credentials into the points where people decide whether to continue.

keyScreens.name: A clearer consultation handoff
keyScreens.description: Reworked the consultation page around a focused form and a straightforward explanation of what happens next.
